description: OWASP RailsGoat (Ruby on Rails 8): the vulnerabilities named by its spec/vulnerabilities suite, wiki tutorial links, and in-code VULNERABILITY comments, pinned to controllers, models, ERB views, config initializers and lib.

vulnerabilities.description: Account update looks up the user with User.where("id = '#{params[:user][:id]}'"), so the hidden user id field allows SQL injection (and updating another account, e.g. the admin).
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/sql_injection_spec.rb; wiki R5-A1-SQL-Injection-Concatentation

vulnerabilities.description: hits_by_ip interpolates the column list into select("#{col}"); admin analytics passes the keys of params[:field] (admin_controller.rb:13-17), so request parameter names become raw SQL.
vulnerabilities.note: RailsGoat wiki A1 SQL Injection (interpolation / analytics) tutorial; confirmed by reading admin_controller#analytics

vulnerabilities.description: Benefit form backup runs system("cp #{full_file_name} ...#{file.original_filename}") with the uploaded file name, giving OS command injection.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/command_injection_spec.rb; wiki A1-Command-Injection

vulnerabilities.description: Login raises "#{email} doesn't exist!", shown to the user as the flash error (sessions_controller.rb:28), enumerating valid accounts.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/broken_auth_spec.rb scenario one; wiki A2-Credential-Enumeration

vulnerabilities.description: Login raises a distinct "Incorrect Password!" error for an existing email, confirming the account exists.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/broken_auth_spec.rb scenario two; wiki A2-Credential-Enumeration

vulnerabilities.description: Password validation only enforces a 6-40 character length, so trivially weak passwords such as "password" are accepted.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/password_complexity_spec.rb; wiki A2-Lack-of-Password-Complexity

vulnerabilities.description: Passwords are stored as unsalted MD5 hashes (Digest::MD5.hexdigest) in the before_save callback.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/password_hashing_spec.rb; wiki A6-Sensitive-Data-Exposure-Insecure-Password-Storage

vulnerabilities.description: Authentication verifies passwords by comparing against an unsalted MD5 digest.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/password_hashing_spec.rb; wiki A6-Sensitive-Data-Exposure-Insecure-Password-Storage

vulnerabilities.description: The header renders current_user.first_name.html_safe, so a first name set via account settings is stored XSS on every page.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/xss_spec.rb; wiki A3-Cross-Site-Scripting; in-code 'VULNERABILITY: XSS via html_safe' comment

vulnerabilities.description: Login page JavaScript document.write()s the decoded location.hash value into the DOM (DOM-based XSS).
vulnerabilities.note: in-code comments 'VULNERABILITY: XSS via URL hash parameter' / 'VULNERABLE: Directly writing user input to DOM'

vulnerabilities.description: The layout emits raw cookies[:font] inside a style block; the cookie is set from params[:font] (dashboard_controller.rb:11), so a crafted link injects markup/script.
vulnerabilities.note: in-code comment 'VULNERABILITY: XSS via cookie font-size'

vulnerabilities.description: download passes params[:name] straight to send_file, so any server file (e.g. config/database.yml) can be downloaded.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/insecure_dor_spec.rb 'attack one'

vulnerabilities.description: download calls params[:type].constantize.new(path), letting the requester choose which Ruby class is instantiated (unsafe reflection).
vulnerabilities.note: same download flaw as insecure_dor_spec.rb 'attack one' (type=File); RailsGoat wiki constantize extra

vulnerabilities.description: Work info is loaded with User.find_by(id: params[:user_id]) instead of current_user, so any user can view another user's salary and SSN.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/insecure_dor_spec.rb 'attack two'; wiki A4-Insecure-Direct-Object-Reference

vulnerabilities.description: The administrative check only runs if params[:admin_id] != "1" (and never for get_user), so any logged-in user can reach /admin/1/* admin functions.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/url_access_spec.rb; wiki A7-Missing-Function-Level-Access-Control--(Admin-Controller)

vulnerabilities.description: protect_from_forgery is commented out (and csrf_meta_tags is commented out in the layout), so state-changing requests such as schedule creation accept cross-site forms.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/csrf_spec.rb; wiki R4-A8-CSRF; 'sea-surfing' code comment

vulnerabilities.description: After login the app does redirect_to path where path is the unvalidated params[:url] (line 12).
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/unvalidated_redirects_spec.rb; wiki A10-Unvalidated-Redirects-and-Forwards-(redirect_to)

vulnerabilities.description: Signup uses params.require(:user).permit!, so a new account can set admin=true.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/mass_assignment_spec.rb 'attack two'; wiki R4-Extras-Mass-Assignment-Admin-Role

vulnerabilities.description: Account update permits :admin, so a user can grant themselves admin via PUT /users/:id.json.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/mass_assignment_spec.rb 'attack one'

vulnerabilities.description: Admin update_user passes params[:user].to_unsafe_h straight to user.update, allowing assignment of any attribute including admin.
vulnerabilities.note: in-code comment 'VULNERABILITY: Using params[:user] directly without strong parameters' citing wiki Extras:-Mass-Assignment-Admin-Role

vulnerabilities.description: The full cleartext SSN is rendered into the page source and only masked client-side by JavaScript; the encrypting before_save in work_info.rb is commented out.
vulnerabilities.note: spec/vulnerabilities/sensitive_data_exposure.rb; wiki A6-Sensitive-Data-Exposure-Cleartext-Storage-SSNs; 'Secure Version' comment next to the line

vulnerabilities.description: secret_key_base is hardcoded in source, letting anyone forge signed/encrypted session cookies.
vulnerabilities.note: docs/bonus_encrypted_secrets.md (hardcoded secret_key_base example); RailsGoat wiki session secret tutorial

vulnerabilities.description: The AES key used for SSNs, bank account numbers and auth tokens is hardcoded.
vulnerabilities.note: in-file comment 'RailsGoat intentionally uses an insecure approach for key management'; docs/bonus_encrypted_secrets.md

vulnerabilities.description: ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT used to derive API tokens (SHA1(salt:id)) is hardcoded, so anyone can mint a valid API token for any user id.
vulnerabilities.note: docs/bonus_encrypted_secrets.md (API keys/secrets); API token logic in api/v1/users_controller.rb:41-43

vulnerabilities.description: The shared encryption routine reuses the hardcoded KEY with a static hardcoded IV (RG_IV), making encryption deterministic across all values.
vulnerabilities.note: code comments 'Added a re-usable encryption routine, shouldn't be an issue!' / 'Should be able to just re-use the same key'

vulnerabilities.description: decrypted_bank_acct_num decrypts any caller-supplied value with the shared key, acting as a decryption oracle (e.g. for other users' bank numbers or auth tokens).
vulnerabilities.note: RailsGoat wiki encryption/logic-flaw extra; same key reuse as lib/encryption.rb comments

vulnerabilities.description: reset_password runs Marshal.load on the base64 'user' request parameter (a hidden field, reset_password.html.erb:13), allowing object injection and resetting any user's password.
vulnerabilities.note: RailsGoat wiki insecure deserialization (A8:2017) tutorial

vulnerabilities.description: The session cookie is configured with httponly: false, so XSS can steal it.
vulnerabilities.note: RailsGoat wiki A2-Lack-of-HttpOnly-Flag

vulnerabilities.description: redos_email matches params[:email] against a nested-quantifier email regex prone to catastrophic backtracking.
vulnerabilities.note: in-code 'VULNERABILITY: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)' comment; wiki R8-A1-ReDoS

vulnerabilities.description: redos_username matches params[:username] against /^(a+)+$/, the canonical exponential-backtracking pattern.
vulnerabilities.note: in-code 'VULNERABILITY: ReDoS with nested quantifiers' comment; wiki R8-A1-ReDoS

vulnerabilities.description: jQuery is loaded from a CDN without a Subresource Integrity attribute.
vulnerabilities.note: in-code comment 'VULNERABILITY A03:2025 - Software Supply Chain Failures ... Missing Subresource Integrity'; tutorials#supply_chain

vulnerabilities.description: The Bootstrap JS bundle is loaded from a CDN without a Subresource Integrity attribute.
vulnerabilities.note: in-code comment 'VULNERABILITY A03:2025 - Software Supply Chain Failures ... Missing Subresource Integrity'; tutorials#supply_chain
